body.v: Three colleagues finished Lesson 1 this week. See the full digest in the ThisIsTea app whenever you like.

hotspots.explain: No password, no deadline and no pressure.
thisistea.example sits right before the first slash, so the link is genuine. You could still skip it and open the app.
It says you can read the digest in the app whenever you like.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: ThisIsTea itself: the domain is exactly thisistea.example.

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: None. There is no deadline and no threat.
choices: None: it is calm and has no deadline

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Nothing: it offers a digest to read. There is no password, no payment and no pressure.
choices: Sign in to keep your password
Nothing, apart from reading a digest

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Even then, you could skip the link and open the ThisIsTea app yourself.
choices: Reply to ask for a longer digest
Open the ThisIsTea app yourself if you want to look

actions.label: Open the ThisIsTea app yourself and read the digest
actions.consequence: The same digest is waiting there.

actions.label: Click the link to read the digest
actions.consequence: It leads to the real domain, so no harm. The app is still the safer habit.

actions.label: Report it to IT as a suspicious email
actions.consequence: IT thanks you and confirms it is genuine. Checking is never wrong, but this one is fine.

attacker_reveal: This one is fine, dear. The domain is exactly thisistea.example, and it asks for nothing. A calm email can be real, and so can one with a link. What matters is who owns the domain and what it wants from you.
